title: Asymptotic exponent of the largest cap set
formal:
Determine, to additive accuracy \(0.01\), the exponent
\[\gamma=\lim_{n\to\infty}\frac{\log_3 M(n)}{n},\]
where \(M(n)\) is the largest size of a subset \(A\subseteq\mathbb F_3^n\) such that \(x+y+z=0\) for \(x,y,z\in A\) implies \(x=y=z\).
definitions: The field \(\mathbb F_3\) has elements 0, 1 and 2 with arithmetic modulo 3; vector addition is coordinatewise. A set satisfying the stated condition is a cap set: it contains no nonconstant three-term arithmetic progression. The logarithm has base 3. Cartesian products of cap sets are cap sets, so \(M(n+m)\ge M(n)M(m)\). Together with \(1\le M(n)\le3^n\), this ensures that the limit exists and equals the supremum of the displayed ratios. For ambient size \(N=3^n\), the maximum is \(N^{\gamma+o(1)}\).
answer_criterion: Output a rational number q and a complete Lean-checked proof that \(|q-\gamma|\le0.01\). Equivalently, prove matching upper and lower bounds trapping gamma in an interval of width at most 0.02 and return its midpoint. A construction alone or the assertion gamma < 1 is insufficient.
why: This asks for the quantitative limit of the polynomial method in additive combinatorics, a source of techniques for algorithms and lower bounds.

context_blocks.text: Ellenberg and Gijswijt proved an exponential saving over the ambient space size. That breakthrough establishes an exponent below one, without determining it.
Tyrrell constructs cap sets of size at least 2.218 to the power n for sufficiently large n. The large gap between construction and upper-bound methods motivates an exponent target.
